name: Question 6
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $10$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5$ defined on $[-5,5).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $10$-periodic extension of $G(x)=-\frac{3}{2}x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5∼-\frac{5}{4}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{75(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

{{field-2}}

Let f(x) be the 10-periodic extension of the function F(x)=−34x2+5 defined on [−5,5). Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the 10-periodic extension of G(x)=−32x from the corresponding Fourier series of f(x).The Fourier series of f(x) is given by
cos⁡(nπx5)
cos⁡(nπx10)
cos⁡(nπx5)
sin⁡(nπx5)
sin⁡(nπx10)
−34x2+5∼−54+∑n=1∞75(−1)n+1n2π2{(cos⁡(nπx10))(S0)}.

Since f is
 
odd
continuous
even
and
 
periodic
piecewise linear
piecewise smooth
on R, we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get
 
75(−1)n+1n2π2
75(−1)nn2π2
15(−1)n+1nπ
15(−1)nnπ
 
cos⁡(nπx5)
sin⁡(nπx5)
−32x∼∑n=1∞{(75(−1)n+1n2π2)(S3)}⋅{(cos⁡(nπx5))(S4)}.
